content: Demeclocycline is an antibiotic that should be taken as prescribed by your healthcare provider. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal effectiveness, it is important to take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow the infection to return. Notify your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Common side effects of demeclocycline may include diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or rectal discomfort. These effects are usually mild and temporary. However, remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, demeclocycline and other tetracycline drugs may cause increased pressure around the brain, a condition known as intracranial hypertension (IH). Women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of IH are at a higher risk. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping the medication, but there is a potential risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms such as persistent headache, vision changes, or nausea. This medication may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition called Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (C. difficile infection). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Symptoms include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, and blood or mucus in the stool. Do not use anti-diarrheal products or opioids if you suspect this condition, as they may worsen the symptoms. Seek medical attention promptly. Prolonged or repeated use of demeclocycline may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Notify your doctor if you notice white patches in your mouth, a change in vaginal discharge, or other symptoms of a fungal infection. Severe allergic reactions to demeclocycline are rare but can occur. Symptoms of a serious allergic reaction include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Seek immediate medical attention if these symptoms occur. Before taking demeclocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other tetracycline medications (such as doxycycline, minocycline, or tetracycline), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Demeclocycline may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccinations. Demeclocycline can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Notify your doctor if you develop sunburn or skin redness. This medication should not be used in children under 8 years of age, as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as demeclocycline may harm an unborn baby. Avoid becoming pregnant while using this medication. Demeclocycline also passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Demeclocycline may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some urine tests for sugar, potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctors that you are using this medication. If someone overdoses on demeclocycline and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Store demeclocycline at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated demeclocycline can result in serious illness. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. If you are using this medication for long-term treatment or to manage SIADH (syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion), regular lab and medical tests (such as complete blood count, kidney/liver function, and mineral levels) should be performed to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
